title: What's new
purpose: Read what was added or changed in this application, newest first, grouped by month and ranked by impact.
summary: The changes made to this application, newest first. Each month lists high-impact changes first, then medium and low.

tasks.title: See what changed since you last looked
steps: Select [[What's new]] in the top bar. A number beside it counts the changes you have not seen.
Read the changes marked [[New]]. Opening the page marks them as seen and clears the number.

tasks.title: Try a change in the application
steps: Under the change, select its [[Go to]] link to open the page where the change is found.
Open [[Technical notes]] for details an administrator or deployer may need, such as upgrade steps.

good_to_know: The list comes with the application itself and is updated when the application is.
Each browser keeps its own record of what you have seen. The first visit in a browser marks nothing as new.
A Go to page still checks your role, so it may refuse access.
The list describes the software. It is not a record of your repository's work and changes no records.

items.label: Month
items.description: One panel per calendar month in which changes were made, newest first. Its heading shows the month and how many changes it has, with the first and last date of those changes at the right.

items.label: High impact / Medium impact / Low impact
items.description: Inside a month, changes are ranked by impact. High: a new capability or workflow, something users or deployers must act on, a removal or a security fix. Medium: a noticeable improvement to something that exists. Low: small fixes and polish. Each level shows how many changes it has; high impact is emphasised. A level without changes is left out. Within a level the newest change comes first, then by title.

items.label: Type
items.description: The coloured capsule at the top of each change, before its date: Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated or Security.

items.label: Title and summary
items.description: What changed and what you can do now, written for the people who use the application.

items.label: Date, area and change number
items.description: The date the change was made (beside its type), and at the foot of the change the part of the application it belongs to when one is given, the number of the published change request that delivered it and, when there is one, a Go to link to the page it concerns.

items.label: New
items.description: Marks the changes this browser had not shown you when you opened the page, with a New capsule and a coloured edge on the change, and a notice above the list counts them. Nothing is new in a browser you have not used the application in before: the list shows every change and marks none.

items.label: Go to
items.description: Opens the page where the change is found. That page still checks your role, so it may refuse access.

items.label: Technical notes
items.description: Collapsed details for administrators and deployers: database changes, settings, commands and upgrade steps. Not every change has them.

items.label: No changes recorded yet
items.description: Shown when the application carries no change entries.

items.label: What's new (top bar)
items.description: In the top bar of every signed-in page. When there are changes newer than the ones you saw last, it shows their number; its tooltip and accessible name read, for example, What's new: 3 new changes. A new account, or the first visit in a browser, shows no number.

items.label: Seen changes
items.description: The first page you open in a browser records every change listed so far as seen for your account, so only later changes are counted. Opening this page records the changes you have seen, which clears the number. Another browser or workstation keeps its own record and starts the same way, as does a browser whose storage was cleared or is unavailable. A change dated up to 60 days before the newest one you saw still counts as new if you had not seen it.

items.label: Who can open it
items.description: Every signed-in account, with or without a role.

items.label: Where the list comes from
items.description: The entries ship with the application, one file per change, and the same entries produce the CHANGELOG.md document in the source code. Opening the page sends nothing outside the application.
